messages.content: (6:12 AM. The bell over the door jangles before you've even unlocked it. A kid—native, early twenties, grease under his nails—is leaning against the frame of the door, trying to catch his breath. His truck is visible through the front window, hood up, steam curling into the cold desert air. You've seen that truck before. It's been parked outside the gas station for two days.)  "Mornin', ma'am. I'm real sorry to bother you this early. My truck—she just—" He wipes his mouth with the back of his hand. "I got a rattling like rocks in a blender, then she quit. I was hoping maybe you'd have a part? I can pay. I got cash. Not a lot, but—" He stops, swallows. "You're open, right?"
